raw_recipe.headline: Ramen Cabbage Salad
raw_recipe.description: In this salad, shredded green cabbage is tossed with dried ramen noodles and nuts in a simple sweet and sour vinaigrette.
raw_recipe.name: Ramen Cabbage Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Toss together the cabbage, noodles and sunflower seeds or almonds.
Whisk together the ramen flavor packet, oil, sugar and vinegar. Pour over cabbage mixture and toss evenly to coat.

review.reviewBody: My grandmother just gave me this recipe and I absolutely love it. Her receipe uses prepackaged coleslaw mix, adds an extra 2 oz. package toasted slivered almonds, and beef flavored ramen. I've eaten this every night this week (I mix it all together right before eating). I make it with 1/2 torn up spinach leave and 1/2 slaw mix to make it a little healthier. Its really tasty with the spinach. However, if serving to guests I would probably skip the spinach b/c it doesn't look as pretty.

This was good, but will let sit overnight to see if flavors intensify. Additions consisted of shredded carrots, a few slices of green pepper, a handful of almonds. toasted the almonds and ramen noodles before adding.

It needed some tweaking, but it was a good base (I already submitted to have a custom recipe made on it). I made it double, so I used a whole head of cabbage and two packages of ramen noodles. I recommend using the Oriental flavor because that matches right. I then, instead of sunflower seeds, used sesame seeds (eyeballed it), used sliced almonds, and also added four chopped green onions. For the dressing, as someone suggested, cut the oil in half, so I left it at a 1/2 cup, used about 5 Tbsp of sugar, and then used 4 tbsp of rice vinegar and 2 tbsp of apple cider vinegar, along with the seasoning packets from the soup package. It came out great and everyone loved it. The thing I didn't do, which I need to do and will do, is add salt and pepper (especially pepper) to taste. I needs that extra flavor and kick. That was added to my customized recipe.
Yum! I usually use a bag of cole slaw or broccoli slaw and change up the vinegar (cider, balsamic, red wine) for variety.
Great recipe. I also add 1/2 cup dried cranberries to the recipe. It makes it even yummier.

I liked this recipe for the versatility. I used the chicken ramen. Prepackaged 
chopped cabbage (purple and green with carrots)added green onion and celery and black pepper.I also used 2w types of olive oil mixed together. My husband wasn't too sure about the ramen but I was. I love the crunch. Pecans also work VERY well instead of sunflower seeds. Great as a summer MEAL!

Oh my! This is fabulous! I used both red & green cabbage, 2 sliced green bell peppers, 1/2 thinly sliced onion, 1/2 white vinegar and 1/2 balsamic vinegar. I didn't have sunflower seeds so I doubled the amount of almonds, which I had toasted. I brought this to a baby shower and it was the first thing to go and EVERYONE wants the recipe! Thank you Tamera for a great recipe!

I bought a bag of already shredded cabbage but didn't know how much to use so I used the whole bag. I think I should have used less because there wasn't enough of the dressing. Next time I'll double the dressing. Otherwise it was very good!

I make something very similiar-- great with leftover chix (shr/chopped) or rotisserie chix-- also use toasted almonds and sesame seeds, but sunflower sounds good too-- mix of red and green cabbage adds visual appeal-- try rice wine vinegar in place of white vinegar. I've never tried it with the seasoning pkt- use a little sugar and white pepper in the dressing instead. Great way to eat cabbage!!!

I followed the recipe the first time and felt it only deserved 4 stars, as it was too oily for my family. The second time I added 1 cup shredded carrots and used only 3 Tablespoon olive oil (instead of 1/2 cup vegetable oil) and it made all the difference in the world. Next time I may try sesame oil and mandarine oranges.

I also used a combination of vinegars, used a package of ready made coleslaw, cut up a little fresh broccoli and added a few craisins for color. Mixed dressing with the seasoning package of chicken ramen. Crushed the noodles and added to salad just before serving. Nice and lite side on Easter Sunday!

Such a great salad. I've been enjoying this salad for many years. I eat it with kalua pork and rice. Sometimes I substitute slivered almonds for the sunflower seeds. In addition I sometimes add a small can of drained mandarin oranges. It's a nice, refreshing addition at times.
We add grilled chicken to ours!

I've made a version of this for years and it's always a family favorite. I add 6 sliced green onions and cilantro to the cabbage and top with the ramen plus slivered almonds and sesame seeds toasted with a bit of butter and sugar. For the dressing, I use rice vinegar, oil and add the ramen packet. I sometimes add chicken for a light summer dinner.

I was having turkey burgers for dinner and wanted some kind of side salad to go with them. I had a half head of cabbage leftover from another recipe, and was looking for a way to use it before it spoiled, and came across this recipe, which was saved in "my saves" in my allrecipes account. Just so happened I had all the ingredients and it had good reviews, so why not? Turned out great, was easy to prepare. The perfect side I was looking for. I used rice vinegar instead of the white vinegar (saw that someone else had in the reviews) but would definitely not use that again. It doesn't have the punch that white vinegar has and that was missing to me. My bad. I did add a Tbsp of Sesame Oil which I thought enhanced the "asian" flavor of this salad. This recipe is great "as is" but creative juices can definitely flow with this one. Thanks allrecipes for another keeper.
So excited to try using gf ramen as I never get to eat this at picnics when others make it with regular ramen. Looks easy!

I’ve made this many times. I doubled up on the ingredients. True. The shelf life is two days tops. The ramen noodles will lose the crispness. I recommend putting in the fridge for at least two hours prior to the initial serving and then a well toss again before serving. Keeping in a glass salad bowl rather than Tupperware which sucks the moisture out of any salads. A standard green salad will last for a week or more if in glass. Plastic wrap over the top since glass bowls haven’t come with lids of any kind.
I added rotisserie chicken and McCormick's salad, toppings, crunchy and flavorful vegetable mix and it's came out good

I added a few dried craisins and used lightly salted almonds and chopped them up myself. I added some salt and pepper to the dressing. But this recipe is good without the additions, too. Everyone loves it!.
I added 1/4n cup of both sunflower seeds and slivered almonds and used a package of coleslaw mix. Yummy.
